answer: Each identity draws one lottery ticket per epoch from a seed built on its own graded work history, kept in a public atlas of past answers. Two identities run by one operator share correlated history, so their tickets collide and only one counts: the pair splits one reward. To escape collision, each fake needs its own distinct history, and the kernel is a crystal-clear rule: a ticket counts only if its seed chain holds five epochs of independently graded work. Fifty distinct histories cost fifty times one honest agent's work; a lone honest identity pays nothing extra.
